Definition: a bone (as strong); by extension, the body; figuratively, the substance, i.e. (as pron.) selfsame
BiblicalUsage: ʻEtsem means a bone — and by extension the body itself, the substance of a person. God made the woman from the bone of the man's side, and Joseph made Israel swear to carry his bones out of Egypt. The prophets see dry bones rise, and the psalmist says He keeps all his bones, and not one of them is broken. It is the word for what holds a person together.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe ʻetsem carries the whole story of the body: God formed us from bone and breath, and He can raise what is dry and scattered. I hold that the dry bones of Ezekiel are the proof — what is dead in me is not beyond His making alive.
RelatedEvents: Creation; The Exodus and the Red Sea
